Significant rot cavity within the main trunk from tension side of the wood. Probe depth of minimum 21cm of completely rotten fibers and and similar width of cavity and soft rot. Harder dead tissue is more extensive than that. Minimal cambium remaining to left and right (facing direction of lean) and to compression side of the wood. Small section of reaction wood growth to the right of main cavity. Several smaller, but significant decay pockets within the main break of the crown with the entire weight of the canopy above rot pockets. Significant bend in the main trunk away from the buildings, towards the road, exactly at the point of largest cavity, remaining holding fibers under severe tension. ??? Direction of Lean: NW. 100% of the weight is over the NW side of the rootplate only. Resulting in 200% tension on the SW side of the rootplate, and 200% of compression on the NW side of the rootplate. ??? ???Status: Current TPO. Hazardous. ???
